speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any other neurological symptoms, such as difficulty speaking, swallowing, or experiencing double vision? Also, do you have a history of cancer or autoimmune disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent fevers, headaches, or vision changes, and have you noticed any new weakness or numbness in your limbs? I would also like to request an MRI of the brain and cervical spine to evaluate for potential demyelinating lesions. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_and_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. MRI Spine: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of non-enhancing multifocal demyelinating lesions are highly characteristic of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), likely triggered by your natalizumab therapy. I am confident in this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
